title: AI Search Optimization
headline: Make your expertise easier to understand and reference.
description: AI search optimization, AEO and GEO services for small businesses. Clear answers, crawlable pages, accurate entities and evidence-led discovery reporting.
intro: Bring answer engine optimization and generative search into a sound SEO program. We make useful business information easier to find, interpret and verify.
deliverables: Business entity and service consistency review
Structured data aligned with visible content

sections.title: Start with the information your buyer needs
sections.body: AI search optimization is useful when customers ask detailed questions about providers, services and alternatives. We identify those questions, review your existing answers and check whether the business information is consistent across your site. The starting point is a clear account of your expertise, actual service area and evidence. A special text file cannot substitute for a useful website.

sections.title: Build answers with enough context
sections.body: An answer should explain the conditions under which advice applies. We organize definitions, comparisons, costs and process questions into readable sections, then support them with real examples and appropriate primary sources. A roofing business might explain the difference between repair and replacement assessments without diagnosing a property it has never inspected. Relevant service and project pages give readers a practical next step.

sections.title: Connect the technical and editorial work
sections.body: We review crawl access, indexability, canonical URLs, navigation and page relationships. Structured data describes information a visitor can actually see. Organization, service and article details should agree instead of presenting different identities to different crawlers. Markdown can provide an additional readable format, but it stays consistent with the main page and does not carry hidden promotional claims.

sections.title: Measure a changing discovery environment
sections.body: We record a repeatable set of relevant questions and note the date, market and platform used for each observation. Responses can vary, so one screenshot is not proof of lasting visibility. Search Console, referral traffic and qualified inquiries help provide context. We separate observed references from traffic and sales rather than attributing every improvement to AI search.

sections.title: Agree on the work, not an inclusion guarantee
sections.body: You receive a prioritized content and technical backlog, the agreed improvements and a review of observable discovery. Google states that its AI search features use foundational SEO requirements, with no special additional optimization required. We do not sell guaranteed mentions, preferred recommendations or a supposed submission shortcut. The proposal defines the websites, topics and implementation allowance covered.

faq: What are AEO and GEO?

Answer engine optimization and generative engine optimization describe work intended to make information useful in answer-based discovery. Our scope connects that work to established SEO, factual business information and helpful content.
Will llms.txt make an AI assistant recommend us?
No file guarantees inclusion or recommendations. A readable content index can assist discovery, but crawl access, useful pages and reliable evidence remain the foundation.
Is this separate from SEO?
It overlaps substantially. We review your existing SEO program first so the same technical work and content are not sold twice.

detail.label: Make your expertise easier to understand and reference.
detail.caption: Bring answer engine optimization and generative search into a sound SEO program. We make useful business information easier to find, interpret and verify.
detail.fit: You already have expertise worth sharing, but the website scatters it across unclear service descriptions and disconnected articles. Customers struggle to find a concise answer, and your team has no consistent way to review answer-based discovery.
detail.outcome: A documented question map, an agreed batch of improved pages and a technical action log. Each recommendation identifies its purpose, supporting evidence and review method so your team can distinguish completed work from an untested hypothesis.
steps: Establish the baseline
Choose representative customer questions and record the current pages that answer them. Review business facts and discovery observations together before selecting the first improvements.
Improve the priority answers
Combine subject expertise, verified evidence and readable page structure. Review the relevant technical tasks alongside the copy so the improved answer has a clear place in the website.
Review and maintain
Compare the same questions and available referral measures at the next review. Record changes in the business or platform context, then decide which answers need clarification or expansion.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Search and AI discovery baseline. Business entity and service consistency review.
A useful review
Completed technical and editorial priorities. Relevant search and AI referral visits.
inputs: Approved business facts and subject experts
metrics: Relevant search and AI referral visits
Qualified inquiries where attribution is available

title: Google Local Services Ads
headline: Turn local interest into a conversation your team can handle.
description: Google Local Services Ads management for eligible businesses. Profile setup support, service-area planning, lead reviews and practical booking reporting.
intro: We help eligible service businesses organize their LSA presence, manage the agreed budget and review the quality of the inquiries they receive.
deliverables: Service types, areas and hours review

sections.title: Check eligibility before allocating spend
sections.body: Local Services Ads availability and screening requirements vary by business category and market. We review the current platform requirements before recommending a launch. The business supplies its own accurate registration, licensing, insurance and verification material when requested. Agency support helps organize the process; it cannot guarantee approval or replace the advertiser’s responsibilities.

sections.title: Describe the jobs and areas you can serve
sections.body: A broad service area may generate inquiries the team cannot handle efficiently. We work with you to define actual coverage, offered job types and operating hours. If the business does not provide emergency service, the profile should not suggest otherwise. Changes in staffing or travel limits belong in the campaign review, not just in an internal dispatch conversation.

sections.title: Prepare the response workflow
sections.body: Lead handling is part of campaign readiness. Decide who answers calls, who checks messages, how missed contacts are followed up and how appointments are recorded. A plumbing company might distinguish urgent repairs from planned water-heater work. Those categories help assess suitability and give the agency useful feedback beyond the platform’s total lead count.

sections.title: Review quality and billing in context
sections.body: We compare platform lead records with your qualification and booking notes. Duplicate contacts, wrong service requests and unanswered inquiries need different actions. Where a billing concern arises, we review the current platform process and available evidence. We do not promise that a disputed inquiry will receive credit or describe historic dispute features as permanent rules.

sections.title: Keep the management scope transparent
sections.body: The starting engagement covers one eligible business profile and an agreed market. You receive a work log, budget review and lead-quality summary. Google’s lead charges are separate from our management fee. Additional profiles, a new CRM connection or wider operational support are quoted before the scope changes.

faq: Is LSA the same as Google Search Ads?
No. They use different account workflows and advertising formats. We compare eligibility, available demand and lead handling before deciding whether to use one or both.
Can you guarantee verification?
No. Google controls screening and approval. We help prepare accurate information and coordinate the steps available to the business.
Is the lead budget included?
No. Platform charges and our management fee are separate. We agree a budget and review cadence before launch.

detail.label: Turn local interest into a conversation your team can handle.
detail.caption: We help eligible service businesses organize their LSA presence, manage the agreed budget and review the quality of the inquiries they receive.
detail.fit: Your business receives local inquiries but lacks a clear picture of which jobs become useful appointments. The profile, operating hours or response process may need attention before additional lead spend can be evaluated sensibly.
detail.outcome: One agreed profile-management process, a reliable lead classification routine and a recurring review of appointments against platform charges. Your team can see what was changed and which operational questions still need an answer.
steps: Prepare the profile
Collect the business facts and requested evidence, then identify outstanding setup steps. Record the services, coverage and budget the business has approved.
Connect the response team
Confirm who receives each inquiry and how outcomes will be recorded. Review sample records with dispatch so suitability and appointment statuses mean the same thing to everyone.
Review and adjust
Compare inquiry types, responses and bookings over an agreed period. Prioritize profile corrections, budget decisions and response-process improvements using the actual records.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Category and market eligibility review. Profile and screening preparation support.
A useful review
Suitable inquiries. Answered and missed contacts.

title: Microsoft Ads Management
headline: Give another search audience a clear route to your business.
description: Microsoft Advertising and Bing Ads management for service businesses. Search campaigns, budget controls, conversion tracking and qualified-lead reviews.
intro: Reach relevant search demand through Microsoft Advertising with a campaign built for your offer, locations and inquiry process.

sections.title: Assess the opportunity before copying an account
sections.body: Microsoft Advertising can complement an existing search program, but it deserves its own budget decision. We review the services you want to promote, the markets you can cover and the evidence available in the account. A working Google campaign provides useful learning, not proof that another channel will deliver the same volume or economics.

sections.title: Build or review the campaign deliberately
sections.body: Campaign groups, keywords and ad messages should reflect distinct service intent. If an import is appropriate, we review the resulting settings, destinations and tracking before launch. An inherited bid, location setting or ad extension can be unsuitable for the new account. We document the configuration so the first performance review has a clear baseline.

sections.title: Make the landing experience consistent
sections.body: Visitors should arrive on a page that matches the service and promise in the ad. We review mobile usability, contact options, service-area information and the inquiry route. A call click and a completed conversation are different outcomes. Tracking design identifies which event is being measured and where sales feedback must provide the rest of the story.

sections.title: Review search quality and operational fit
sections.body: Search terms, audience settings and available placement information help explain where budget is going. Your team’s qualification notes add the business context. A campaign can appear efficient while attracting work you cannot fulfill. We agree a review rhythm and use evidence to adjust exclusions, messaging and budget instead of treating every fluctuation as a reason to rebuild.

sections.title: Expand only after the test answers its question
sections.body: A first scope can focus on one account, one market and a defined service group. The review separates management fees, media spend and any landing-page work. Where the channel produces suitable opportunities within your agreed economics, we can discuss expansion. Where it does not, the report should make the limitations and next decision clear.

faq: Do you also call this Bing Ads?
Yes. Bing Ads is a familiar search term for Microsoft Advertising. We clarify the actual campaign types and distribution included in your proposal.
Can you import our Google Ads campaigns?
Where suitable, an import can help with setup. We still review settings, copy, tracking and destinations before launch.
Will Microsoft leads cost less?
That depends on the market, account and lead quality. We evaluate your actual qualified outcomes rather than promise a lower cost.

detail.label: Give another search audience a clear route to your business.
detail.caption: Reach relevant search demand through Microsoft Advertising with a campaign built for your offer, locations and inquiry process.
detail.fit: You want to test another search channel without losing sight of acquisition cost or lead quality. The business has a defined service, a usable destination page and someone available to review the inquiries that follow.
detail.outcome: A clearly configured search account, documented conversion definitions and a practical review of whether this channel deserves further investment. The test produces evidence for a decision, including limitations where the volume is small.
steps: Frame the channel test
Record the market, service, test budget and qualification criteria. Review existing search learning and decide what can transfer to the new account.
Launch with checks
Build or review the campaigns, validate destinations and confirm tracking. Keep a configuration record so later changes can be compared with the launch baseline.
Assess suitable opportunities
Combine account performance with sales feedback. Identify wasted searches, useful demand and operational limits before proposing a budget increase.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Account and opportunity review. Search campaign structure and copy.
A useful review
Relevant search traffic. Successful inquiry events.

title: LinkedIn Ads Management
headline: Reach the professional buyer behind the next opportunity.
description: LinkedIn Ads management for B2B and commercial-service businesses. Audience planning, creative, lead forms and reporting tied to qualified opportunities.
intro: Build a focused campaign for business buyers, commercial decision-makers and partners whose needs match your offer.
deliverables: Lead form or landing-page setup review

sections.title: Use the channel for a specific business audience
sections.body: LinkedIn campaigns are most useful to assess when the buyer’s professional role matters. A commercial contractor reaching property decision-makers has a different brief from a residential emergency service. We identify the buying roles, company context, problem and credible offer before proposing a campaign. A broad professional audience alone is not a sufficient targeting strategy.

sections.title: Offer something that fits the buying stage
sections.body: An unfamiliar prospect may need a useful planning resource, a relevant project explanation or a consultation with a clearly stated purpose. We align creative, copy and the destination around one offer. Claims about project outcomes require evidence. A lead magnet should be genuinely useful instead of hiding a thin sales pitch behind a long form.

sections.title: Build a reliable form and follow-up route
sections.body: We define the information needed for a useful first conversation and review the permissions required to retrieve leads. Native forms and website forms each need a tested handoff to the person responsible for follow-up. The confirmation message should explain what happens next. Any integration, email sequence or CRM work is itemized in the scope.

sections.title: Judge opportunities beyond the submission
sections.body: Professional targeting does not guarantee that every respondent has purchasing authority or an active project. We agree qualification categories with your sales team and review fit, response, meeting outcomes and pipeline progress. Longer commercial buying cycles require a different evaluation window from an urgent consumer service. Reporting should state those limits instead of presenting every download as a sale.

sections.title: Keep the test focused and reviewable
sections.body: The initial program covers an agreed account, audience and creative allowance. Media spend is separate, and larger creative or integration requirements are priced explicitly. We record the hypothesis and stopping conditions before launch. The next step may be a new message, a narrower audience, a stronger offer or a decision to prioritize another channel.

faq: Is LinkedIn suitable for home services?
It can be relevant to commercial contracts, property relationships or B2B partnerships. A residential service should not assume it is the best first acquisition channel.
Do you handle lead forms?
Yes, within the agreed setup and routing scope. Account access, lead permissions and the follow-up owner need to be confirmed.
Are sales appointments guaranteed?
No. We agree on campaign work, measurement and qualification criteria. Buyers decide whether to engage.

detail.label: Reach the professional buyer behind the next opportunity.
detail.caption: Build a focused campaign for business buyers, commercial decision-makers and partners whose needs match your offer.
detail.fit: Your ideal buyer is a professional decision-maker, but existing marketing is aimed at a broad consumer audience. You need an offer and qualification process that reflect the longer conversation behind a commercial purchase.
detail.outcome: A campaign brief, approved creative and a tested lead handoff for one professional audience. Reporting follows the agreed stages from response to meaningful sales opportunity, with the buying cycle made explicit.
steps: Define the buying role
Identify who experiences the problem, who influences the decision and what information each needs. Choose one audience and a useful first offer.
Prepare the campaign journey
Align the creative, form and confirmation with the offer. Test access to lead records and confirm the person responsible for the first response.
Learn from sales feedback
Review fit, replies and meeting outcomes alongside campaign metrics. Use the findings to improve the audience definition or offer before expanding the program.
checks: An agreed starting scope
B2B audience and offer workshop. Campaign and creative planning.
A useful review
Audience and offer fit. Qualified form submissions.

title: Email Marketing
headline: Keep the conversation going with people who want to hear from you.
description: Email marketing for small businesses and service companies. Newsletter planning, lifecycle messages, audience segmentation and measurable website journeys.
intro: Connect useful content and timely offers with an audience you have permission to contact. We plan the message, build the campaign and review the response.

sections.title: Start with the relationship, not a purchased list
sections.body: A useful email program begins with how contacts joined, what they expect and which messages are appropriate. We review the audience source, existing preferences and unsubscribe process before proposing a campaign. Customer reminders, active prospects and newsletter readers should not automatically receive identical messages. Your business remains responsible for confirming its permissions and applicable requirements.

sections.title: Choose the purpose of each sequence
sections.body: A newsletter shares useful expertise; an estimate follow-up answers outstanding questions; a maintenance reminder helps an existing customer plan. We map the trigger, intended reader, message and next action for each use case. This prevents a complicated automation from becoming a series of disconnected promotions. The initial scope concentrates on a manageable set of messages.

sections.title: Write for a specific decision
sections.body: Email copy should make the reason for contacting the reader clear. A landscaping reminder might explain seasonal scheduling and link to the relevant service page. A remodeler could answer planning questions after an inquiry. Subject lines and previews need to match the message. Any prices, deadlines or capacity claims are approved by the business rather than added for artificial urgency.

sections.title: Check the complete delivery journey
sections.body: We review templates at mobile size, test links and forms, and confirm the landing page follows through on the offer. Audience selections and suppression rules are checked before an approved send. Sender setup and platform access are reviewed within the technical scope. Integration problems receive their own estimate when they require development beyond campaign production.

sections.title: Review responses and list health together
sections.body: Clicks, replies, inquiries and unsubscribes provide different kinds of feedback. Open-rate data can be affected by privacy features, so it should not carry the entire evaluation. We agree campaign tags and conversion events, then review whether useful website actions or conversations followed. The reporting distinguishes observed outcomes from assumptions about attribution.

faq: Will you buy or scrape mailing lists?
No. We work from a documented audience and permission process supplied by the business.
Can you create automated follow-ups?
Yes. We agree the triggers, exclusions, messages and integration requirements before building a sequence.
Is software included?
Email platform subscriptions, specialized deliverability services and custom integrations are separate unless the proposal explicitly includes them.

detail.label: Keep the conversation going with people who want to hear from you.
detail.caption: Connect useful content and timely offers with an audience you have permission to contact. We plan the message, build the campaign and review the response.
detail.fit: You have an existing audience or customer list but no dependable rhythm for useful communication. Messages may be written at the last minute, sent to everyone or disconnected from the website and sales process.
detail.outcome: An approved campaign calendar, reusable production process and reporting that explains useful responses. Your team knows which messages are going out, why each audience receives them and who handles the next conversation.
steps: Map audience and purpose
Review how contacts joined and what they expect. Choose the first campaign goal, destination and audience segment before drafting copy.
Produce and approve
Prepare the message and layout, check facts and links, and collect one consolidated approval. Record the selected audience and suppression checks before release.
Review the response
Connect campaign activity with replies, website actions and list-health signals. Use those observations to decide the next message rather than repeat an unhelpful promotion.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Audience and permission review. Newsletter and lifecycle planning.
A useful review
Useful clicks and replies. Inquiries tied to campaign links.

title: Reputation Management
headline: Make genuine customer feedback part of how you improve.
description: Reputation management for service businesses. Ethical review requests, response workflows, profile consistency and reporting grounded in real customer feedback.
intro: Build a practical process for requesting feedback, responding thoughtfully and keeping public business information accurate.
deliverables: Review monitoring within an agreed scope
Monthly feedback themes and action log

sections.title: Understand where trust breaks down
sections.body: Customers may find inconsistent hours, unanswered reviews or confusing service information before reaching your website. We inventory the relevant public profiles and identify which issues affect their decision. A reputation program should connect marketing with operational feedback. If repeated complaints describe missed calls or unclear estimates, the underlying process needs attention alongside the public response.

sections.title: Ask real customers without filtering by sentiment
sections.body: We help define a neutral request process for eligible customers after an appropriate service milestone. The process should not ask only happy customers to review publicly while hiding everyone else in a private route. No fabricated reviews, paid positive ratings or invented customer identities are included. Requests should explain the action simply and respect the platform’s current rules.

sections.title: Respond with care and protect private information
sections.body: A response can acknowledge the issue and explain the next step without exposing job details, payment information or personal circumstances. We prepare response guidance and identify situations that require the business owner’s review. Serious complaints may need direct resolution outside the public thread. Templates support consistency, but the final response should address what the person actually said.

sections.title: Keep profiles accurate as the business changes
sections.body: Service areas, hours, links and contact information need a named owner. We review the profiles included in your scope and record changes so future updates do not contradict each other. We do not invent additional offices or promise review removal. A platform-policy issue is assessed against the available evidence and the platform’s reporting process.

sections.title: Turn feedback into useful work
sections.body: The monthly review separates profile corrections, response activity and recurring customer themes. A stronger request process does not establish that service quality has improved, so we discuss operational observations with your team. You receive an action log and priorities for the next cycle. The aim is reliable business information and an accountable feedback process that customers can trust.

faq: Can you remove negative reviews?
We can assess whether a review appears to breach platform policy and help use the available reporting process. The platform decides removal. We cannot erase legitimate criticism.
Do you write customer reviews?
No. Customers supply their own genuine experience. We help with neutral requests and business responses.
Can you work across several locations?
Yes. Each real location and profile needs an agreed scope, accurate information and a response owner.

detail.label: Make genuine customer feedback part of how you improve.
detail.caption: Build a practical process for requesting feedback, responding thoughtfully and keeping public business information accurate.
detail.fit: Customer feedback exists across several profiles, yet nobody owns the complete process. Review requests are inconsistent, responses stall and recurring concerns are not reaching the people who can resolve them.
detail.outcome: A neutral request workflow, response responsibilities and a recurring action log. The engagement makes public business information easier to maintain and turns feedback themes into specific questions for your operations team.
steps: Inventory the public picture
Identify the profiles customers encounter and record accuracy or response gaps. Confirm authorized access and the owner of each business fact.
Put the workflow in place
Agree when neutral requests are appropriate and how responses are reviewed. Prepare an escalation path for sensitive issues that require direct attention.
Close the feedback loop
Review recurring concerns with the business owner. Track profile corrections and agreed operational actions, not only the quantity of new reviews.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Review and profile baseline. Neutral customer feedback request workflow.
A useful review
Profile accuracy. Response coverage and timeliness.

title: Conversion Rate Optimization
headline: Find the friction between interest and inquiry.
description: Conversion rate optimization for business websites. Journey research, form improvements, measurement checks and experiments matched to real traffic levels.
intro: Use evidence to improve the path from a relevant visit to a useful conversation. We review the journey before deciding what to change.

sections.title: Define the outcome before judging the page
sections.body: A conversion could be a submitted form, a completed purchase or a booked consultation. These are not interchangeable, and some events can fire without a successful business outcome. We audit the existing measurement and agree the primary action before comparing pages. The baseline includes traffic source, device, service intent and the available lead-quality feedback.

sections.title: Find friction in the actual customer journey
sections.body: We review the offer, navigation, page content, form fields and confirmation process. A visitor may understand the service but be unable to judge the price range or next step. Mobile usability can reveal problems hidden by a spacious desktop layout. Where recordings or research tools are appropriate, we agree the privacy settings and interpretation before collecting data.

sections.title: Prioritize changes by evidence and effort
sections.body: A broken form should be fixed before testing subtle button variations. We organize proposed changes by their supporting evidence, likely relevance and implementation cost. Clearer service-area information, useful proof or a shorter form can each address a different concern. The plan records the expected mechanism so a later review can explain why the change did or did not help.

sections.title: Use an evaluation method that fits the traffic
sections.body: A low-volume website may not support a quick, reliable A/B test. In that case, usability checks and carefully documented sequential changes can still improve the experience, with appropriate caution about attribution. When an experiment is feasible, we specify the hypothesis, primary measure, audience and review criteria in advance rather than selecting a favorable result afterward.

sections.title: Connect conversion rate with business quality
sections.body: More submissions are not necessarily better if the additional inquiries are irrelevant. We review qualification, appointments and sales feedback alongside the page conversion measure. A higher rate during a promotion or seasonal peak does not prove the design caused the change. The deliverable is a documented learning and improvement process, with implementation hours and experiments defined in the proposal.

faq: Is CRO only changing button colors?
No. The work can include offer clarity, page structure, forms, evidence, performance and measurement. We prioritize the problem before choosing a design treatment.
Can you test a low-traffic website?
We can improve it, but a statistically meaningful split test may require more traffic or time than the site has. We explain the limits and choose a suitable review method.
Do you guarantee a percentage increase?
No. Any target is a planning assumption. We report the observed result with its period, context and measurement limits.

detail.label: Find the friction between interest and inquiry.
detail.caption: Use evidence to improve the path from a relevant visit to a useful conversation. We review the journey before deciding what to change.
detail.fit: Your site receives relevant visitors, but the reasons they stop short of contacting you are unclear. You need a prioritized explanation of the friction before commissioning another redesign or spending more to bring people to the same journey.
detail.outcome: A measurement check and a ranked improvement backlog with the evidence behind each recommendation. Depending on the agreed scope, the next phase may be implementation, user research or a properly specified experiment.
steps: Establish a reliable baseline
Confirm the primary action and inspect how it is recorded. Compare the relevant devices, traffic sources and service journeys before interpreting a blended rate.
Investigate the friction
Review the offer, information gaps, form behavior and mobile experience. Document observations and distinguish confirmed defects from ideas that still need testing.
Evaluate the improvement
Use the method suited to the available traffic and business cycle. Record the change, observation window, outcome and limits before choosing another test.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Conversion measurement and journey review. Mobile and form usability audit.
A useful review
Successful primary actions. Qualified inquiry rate.

title: Lead Generation
headline: Connect your marketing with the work you actually want.
description: Lead generation services for small businesses and home-service companies. Connected campaigns, landing pages, qualification and follow-up reporting.
intro: Bring the offer, acquisition channel and response process into one plan. We focus on suitable opportunities and a clear handoff to your team.
deliverables: Form, call and CRM handoff review

sections.title: Decide what a useful lead means
sections.body: A business can attract inquiries and still struggle to fill the right jobs. We define the priority service, real coverage, project fit and delivery capacity before choosing a channel. The definition includes exclusions such as unsupported locations or work below your minimum scope. This creates a shared basis for evaluating marketing rather than arguing about whether every contact counts.

sections.title: Match the offer to the buying journey
sections.body: Urgent demand, planned purchases and longer commercial projects need different messages. Search advertising may address an active need; social campaigns can introduce an offer; organic content can answer questions over time. We choose a starting combination based on the business and available evidence. More channels add coordination work and should have a specific purpose.

sections.title: Build the path from interest to a record
sections.body: The ad or article, landing page, form and confirmation should describe the same offer. We review whether a successful inquiry reaches the right inbox or system with enough context to respond. Source tags and qualification fields are designed to help decisions, not burden visitors with an unnecessary questionnaire. Custom integrations are defined before implementation begins.

sections.title: Give follow-up a named owner
sections.body: A campaign cannot compensate for every missed call or unanswered email. We agree who receives inquiries, how the team records contact attempts and which status changes matter. Estimates, appointments and sales need consistent definitions. For a remodeler, for example, a useful consultation request and an accepted project are separate milestones with different time windows.

sections.title: Review cost with the full business context
sections.body: Reports distinguish raw inquiries, qualified opportunities, appointments and customers where reliable data exists. Media fees, management and other delivery costs should be visible when assessing acquisition economics. We do not promise a fixed number of leads or guaranteed revenue. The proposal defines channels, markets, creative allowances and the operational responsibilities required to run the program.

faq: Do you sell shared contact lists?
Our service focuses on campaigns and inquiry journeys for your business. Any different acquisition arrangement would require its own explicit scope and source review.
Do you charge per lead?
Our published starting scopes use project or monthly fees. Any different commercial arrangement must define qualification, attribution and terms in a written proposal.
Can we use our current CRM?
We review the available integration and permissions. A simple routing change and a custom system connection require different implementation scopes.

detail.label: Connect your marketing with the work you actually want.
detail.caption: Bring the offer, acquisition channel and response process into one plan. We focus on suitable opportunities and a clear handoff to your team.
detail.fit: Your marketing channels produce contacts, but the team cannot agree which ones fit the business or where opportunities are being lost. You need a shared acquisition and follow-up plan around services you can actually deliver.
detail.outcome: A defined lead journey with qualification rules, responsible owners and useful reporting. Campaign work and operational handoffs are connected so the next review can locate problems between the first click and a sales conversation.
steps: Define the opportunity
Agree priority work, coverage, exclusions and capacity. Set the initial channel and qualification criteria using the information already available.
Connect capture and response
Review the destination, form or call route and receiving system. Test a realistic inquiry and confirm the team can act on its context.
Review the full path
Compare inquiries, qualification and appointment outcomes. Separate a campaign mismatch from a slow response or unavailable service before changing the budget.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Service and market opportunity brief. Lead definition and qualification rules.
A useful review
Qualified opportunities. Contact and appointment rates.

title: Digital Media Buying
headline: Put your message in the right context, with a clear media plan.
description: Digital media buying for growing businesses. Programmatic display, streaming TV and video campaign planning with clear inventory, creative and measurement scope.
intro: Plan display, video and streaming TV advertising around a real audience, approved creative and a transparent buying arrangement.
deliverables: Programmatic, display or CTV media plan

sections.title: Choose the format for the job it needs to do
sections.body: Display, streaming TV and online video can support awareness, consideration or remarketing, but they are not interchangeable with high-intent search. We review the offer, audience, available creative and existing acquisition program before recommending a media mix. A campaign should have a defined role and budget rather than simply add another logo to the marketing plan.

sections.title: Make the buying arrangement understandable
sections.body: The proposal identifies the platform or buying partner, available markets, planned inventory and management responsibilities. Programmatic buying describes a method of purchasing inventory, not a promise of superior customers. We review available suitability controls and exclusions with you. Access, minimum budgets and formats depend on the selected platform and are confirmed before an agreement is made.

sections.title: Prepare the creative and the destination together
sections.body: A video placement needs an approved asset in the correct format, a clear message and an appropriate next step. A display campaign may need several sizes and a relevant landing page. We list these production requirements before launch. Filming, voiceovers, licensing and substantial animation are separate deliverables unless explicitly included in the creative scope.

sections.title: Measure reach and response without overstating attribution
sections.body: We distinguish delivery measures such as impressions and reach from visits, inquiries and sales. View-through reporting needs particular care because an exposed person may later convert for another reason. The measurement brief records the attribution window and available limitations. Where feasible, we discuss comparison approaches and whether the budget is sufficient to learn something useful.

sections.title: Review distribution as well as aggregate results
sections.body: Reporting should show the available inventory and audience breakdown, not only a blended total. We assess the agreed placement controls, frequency, creative response and website actions. The next budget decision follows the purpose of the campaign. Emerging ad channels are evaluated individually; no platform access, beta invitation or unsupported ad format is promised.

faq: Do you manage programmatic and streaming TV ads?
Yes, subject to a suitable platform, market, budget and creative scope. The proposal identifies the actual inventory and buying arrangement.
Is video production included?
It is quoted separately unless listed in the agreed scope. We confirm asset specifications before media is booked.
Can you run ads on a new AI platform?
We first verify that the platform supports the advertiser, geography and campaign type. We do not sell access to unavailable inventory or claim a special platform relationship.

detail.label: Put your message in the right context, with a clear media plan.
detail.caption: Plan display, video and streaming TV advertising around a real audience, approved creative and a transparent buying arrangement.
detail.fit: You have an approved offer and creative assets, and want to assess formats beyond your existing search or social activity. The next step needs a clear purpose, transparent media costs and an explanation of what the reporting can establish.
detail.outcome: A media brief identifying the selected inventory, creative requirements, responsibilities and evaluation method. Delivery reporting shows the available distribution details and distinguishes observed response from attributed or estimated effects.

Prepare assets and controls

title: Franchise & Multi-Location Marketing
headline: Give every location a clear place in the bigger picture.
description: Franchise and multi-location marketing services. Shared brand standards, local campaign planning, location content and reporting across real service markets.
intro: Connect central brand direction with the services, coverage and operating capacity of each real location.

sections.title: Separate central decisions from local responsibilities
sections.body: A franchise or multi-location business needs clarity about who approves offers, pays for media and handles inquiries. We begin with the operating structure rather than copying one campaign across every territory. Shared brand requirements and location-specific facts are recorded separately. This prevents a national promotion from advertising a service a particular branch does not provide.

sections.title: Build a useful location information system
sections.body: Each real location needs accurate contact details, service coverage, hours and relevant evidence. We organize page templates and profile responsibilities so local information can be maintained consistently. A page should help a customer choose the right branch. It should not invent an office, testimonial or local team merely to create another search landing page.

sections.title: Plan budgets around capacity and market conditions
sections.body: Different locations may have different service priorities, available staff and demand. We document the initial allocation and the evidence used to review it. Shared advertising accounts and separate local accounts each create operational considerations. The proposal states the chosen structure, permissions and responsibilities so reporting and handoff remain understandable.

sections.title: Route inquiries to a responsible team
sections.body: A national form is only useful if the right branch receives the inquiry and knows what to do next. We review routing rules, territory overlap, missing-location cases and the feedback needed to qualify opportunities. Where a CRM integration is required, the technical work is scoped separately. A test submission should confirm the actual destination before a campaign expands.

sections.title: Roll out in stages and compare like with like
sections.body: An initial group of locations can reveal content, routing and approval problems before wider rollout. Reporting separates individual markets and explains differences in services, budgets and periods. A blended average can hide an underperforming branch or a capacity issue. The deliverable is a repeatable operating plan with clear local exceptions, not a promise that every market will perform identically.

faq: Do all locations get identical pages?
No. Templates can share a design, but actual services, coverage, contact information and useful local evidence should be accurate for each location.
Can you work with both a head office and franchisees?
Yes. We agree who approves work, owns accounts, pays invoices and handles local decisions before starting.
How is this priced?
We scope the number of markets, platforms, page types and reporting requirements. A rollout proposal itemizes central setup and ongoing location work.

detail.label: Give every location a clear place in the bigger picture.
detail.caption: Connect central brand direction with the services, coverage and operating capacity of each real location.
detail.fit: Your brand operates across real locations with different staff, territories and service priorities. Central assets help, but local facts, approvals and inquiry routing need a reliable system to prevent contradictory marketing.
detail.outcome: A rollout framework that separates shared brand work from each location’s responsibilities. Page standards, campaign ownership and reporting definitions make additional markets easier to introduce without losing the local context customers need.
steps: Map the operating model
Document locations, territory rules, approvers and account ownership. Identify the differences that must survive a shared template or campaign structure.
Pilot the approach
Choose an initial group of locations and test the content, approval and routing process. Resolve gaps before expanding the same system across the network.
Compare and roll out
Review comparable measures by market and record justified local exceptions. Use the pilot findings to improve the next release group.

title: AI Workflow & Automation
headline: Give repeatable work a clearer process, then automate what fits.
description: AI workflow and automation services for small businesses. Process mapping, supported integrations, human review and tested handoffs for routine operations.
intro: Reduce repetitive handling with a carefully scoped workflow. We connect the right systems and keep people responsible for decisions that need judgment.
deliverables: Defined inputs, outputs and exception paths

sections.title: Start with a specific operational problem
sections.body: An automation project should name the task, its owner and the cost of getting it wrong. Examples include organizing approved content drafts, routing inquiry records or preparing a summary for a team member to review. We map the current process before choosing a tool. A poorly defined workflow becomes harder to understand when automation is added around it.

sections.title: Choose what the system can decide and what people approve
sections.body: Deterministic rules are often appropriate for known routing conditions. An AI-assisted step may help with text organization or classification, but its output needs an evaluation method and an exception path. We identify where a human must confirm facts, approve a message or resolve ambiguity. The brief does not assume that every repetitive task needs a language model.

sections.title: Connect systems with appropriate access
sections.body: The implementation uses the supported permissions and integration methods available in your systems. We agree which information the workflow needs and where it is processed. Credentials are managed through the deployment environment rather than exposed in public content. Platform subscriptions and model usage are separate costs unless explicitly included in the proposal.

sections.title: Test the cases that interrupt ordinary work
sections.body: A successful demonstration is only one scenario. We test missing fields, duplicate records, rejected permissions, slow responses and unexpected input where relevant. The workflow needs a visible error state and a named owner for unresolved items. For AI-assisted steps, a representative evaluation set helps establish whether the outputs are useful enough for the intended task.

sections.title: Make the handoff and ongoing costs visible
sections.body: You receive documentation of the workflow, dependencies, permissions and operating procedure within the agreed scope. Monitoring, later model changes and new integrations are discussed separately. We do not promise a fully autonomous employee or savings that have not been measured. A useful automation should leave your team able to understand what happened and intervene when needed.

faq: Can you automate lead routing or content preparation?
Yes, after reviewing the systems, access and exception handling required. We agree which actions can run automatically and which need review.
Are AI outputs always accurate?
No. Workflows need suitable evaluation, human review and failure handling. The design should reflect the consequences of an incorrect output.
Are software and model fees included?
They are listed separately unless the proposal includes a defined allowance. We estimate usage assumptions before implementation.

detail.label: Give repeatable work a clearer process, then automate what fits.
detail.caption: Reduce repetitive handling with a carefully scoped workflow. We connect the right systems and keep people responsible for decisions that need judgment.
detail.fit: A recurring task moves between tools and people with too much manual copying or unclear handoffs. You need to understand the workflow and its failure cases before deciding whether rules, integrations or an AI-assisted step will help.
detail.outcome: A scoped working automation with documented permissions, review points and exception handling. The handoff explains how to operate it, where to inspect failures and which ongoing usage or support costs remain.
steps: Specify the task
Map the current inputs, decisions, systems and outputs. Agree the person responsible for exceptions and choose representative examples for evaluation.
Build a controlled pilot
Implement the smallest useful workflow with appropriate access. Test ordinary inputs, ambiguous cases and failures before expanding the automation’s responsibilities.
Evaluate and hand over
Review output quality and operating effort against the baseline. Document limitations, monitoring and intervention steps so the team can use the workflow confidently.
checks: An agreed starting scope
Process and system discovery. Defined inputs, outputs and exception paths.
A useful review
Completed and failed workflow runs. Exception handling quality.
metrics: Measured operating effort and usage costs
